messages:
matt: Quick follow-up on the ingress congestion thing — I sketched a lightweight protocol we could use across edge/gateway to degrade gracefully under overload. 3 modes: SHED (reject low-priority), DEGRADE (partial streaming / truncated responses), REDIRECT (fallback to cheaper model/region). Short sketch below, please react with :thumbsup: or concerns.

anya: love the framing. how do we decide priority? token-level? route-level?

matt: priority comes from route + token budget + per-tenant SLA. basic policy: if tenant has >= committed qps, no shed. else use route_priority (low/med/high) + ephemeral score.

kevin: two quick concerns:
- streaming resume/cutoff semantics (clients expect a partial stream vs a hard abort)
- billing/metrics: we need clear markers to avoid charging for truncated tokens.

liara: for streaming resume: suggest we add a short handshake trailer with \`X-Rw-Degrade: <mode>;reason=<code>\` so client lib can surface "trimmed" vs "failed". also put `degraded=true` in trace/span.

matt: agreed. example header: 
```
X-Rw-Degrade: DEGRADE;reason=ingress_congestion;method=truncate
```
Client behaviour: if DEGRADE+truncate -> show partial content with a soft badge; if SHED -> fall back to cached response or show error.

danielle: on implementation: where does decision live? edge or gateway? my vote: edge makes fast local decision with policy sync from control plane. gateway can override with longer-term insights (cost, model availability).

anya: local edge decisions need to be deterministic to avoid flapping. we should expose a small token-bucket state and a monotonically increasing "degrade-epoch" header so downstream can detect policy shifts.

kevin: about retries: we MUST avoid transparent retries that convert a SHED into duplicate side-effects. retry policy should be: idempotent-only and honor degrade header. plus a backoff multiplier tied to queue-latency percentile.

liara: sample ingress rule snippet (proto-ish):
```yaml
- route: /v1/generate
  priority: medium
  degrade_policies:
    - threshold_p50_ms: 200
      action: DEGRADE
    - threshold_p99_ms: 1000
      action: SHED
  fallback: cheaper-model: redwood/mini-1
```

matt: ops note: when we DEGRADE we should also emit a small synthetic token (0-cost marker) so billing pipeline can attribute. that avoids accidental charges when we truncate the stream.

sre-bot: deployed ingress-congestion-proto branch to staging :rocket: (staging/edge-02)

danielle: do we want canary rollouts of the policy sync? yes. control-plane will send rollout_id and epoch in the header. idea: rollout gradually by region then tenant-size.

anya: thought: for low-latency interactive routes we could opt for "micro-degrade" where we continue streaming but switch to compressed-format tokens (paraphrase) to preserve latency at lower cost. implementation complexity is higher but could be high ROI.

kevin: paraphrase switching raises model-consistency concerns. determinism problems when clients re-request missing context. need clear contract: paraphrase outputs are not canonical.

matt: next steps i propose:
- prototype edge-side fast policy evaluator (C++)
- add `X-Rw-Degrade` header + trace tags
- gating: start with SHED+DEGRADE, postpone REDIRECT until fallback infra is tested
- plan a 1-week staged test against synthetic overload scenarios

liara: i'll take the header + trace bits. danielle want to own rollout orchestration?

danielle: yep -- will draft rollout plan and tenant selection criteria.

matt: perfect. will open RFC follow-up PR with config shapes + test plan. thanks all.

kevin: one more nit: add a canned error code set so we don't re-invent reason strings (`INGRESS_SHED`, `DEGRADE_TRUNCATED`, `REDIRECT_FALLBACK`).

matt: noted. will include codes.

anya: :thumbsup:

sre-bot: test-run 2026-03-21 10:12 — synthetic p99 injected, DEGRADE triggered on /v1/generate for tenant acme-inc

matt: cool — will check logs and summary tomorrow. thanks everyone.
